# Specifically Programmed Computer Server System for Media and Web Tracking Data Attribution

## Overview

The present invention discloses a specifically programmed computer server system architected to process, correlate, and analyze media broadcast data alongside web-based tracking transaction data through a series of purpose-configured functional modules. This system addresses the technical challenge of establishing verifiable attribution links between media airings—such as television advertisements or other broadcast creatives—and resulting consumer actions captured through web-based transaction channels.

## System Architecture and Data Acquisition

The server system is configured to periodically obtain media data over a computer network from a plurality of media data sources. This media data is associated with multiple media airings corresponding to various creatives that have been broadcast or otherwise disseminated across one or more media channels. Each media airing record within this dataset typically encompasses information such as the airing timestamp, the media outlet or channel through which the creative was broadcast, the identity of the specific creative, and other metadata relevant to establishing a temporal and contextual profile of when and how the creative was presented to potential consumers.

In parallel with the media data acquisition process, the server system is further configured to periodically collect web tracking transaction data from a web tracking electronic source. This web tracking data captures granular metrics pertaining to web-originated activities, including but not limited to orders placed by consumers in direct or indirect response to offers presented within the creatives. Each transactional web data record may include information such as order timestamps, order identifiers, transaction values, and other data points indicative of consumer engagement with the offer presented through the media airing.

## Attribution Processing Module

A core functional component of the disclosed system is its attribution engine, which is specifically configured to process each web order record contained within the transactional web data and determine its corresponding media airing. For each individual web order, the server system executes a matching or correlation process that evaluates the temporal proximity, offer identifiers, promotional codes, or other associative data points between the web order and the pool of available media airing records. Through this process, the system attributes the specific web order to the media airing that most plausibly or definitively triggered the consumer action, thereby establishing a causal or correlative link between the broadcast event and the resulting transaction.

## Real-Time Reporting Module

Upon completion of the data processing and attribution operations, the server system is further configured to generate a web attribution report that reflects the correlations established between media airings and web orders. Notably, this report is designed to be updatable in real-time, meaning that as new media data and web tracking transaction data continue to be acquired and processed by the system, the attribution report is dynamically refreshed to reflect the most current state of the underlying data. The system then displays this real-time updatable report, for instance, through a user interface accessible to operators, advertisers, or other stakeholders, thereby providing continuous visibility into the effectiveness and performance of media airings in driving web-based consumer transactions.

## Technical Advantages

This specifically programmed server architecture provides several technical advantages over conventional systems, including the ability to process high volumes of heterogeneous data from disparate sources in a periodic and automated fashion, the capacity to perform granular, order-level attribution analysis rather than relying on aggregate or estimated correlations, and the provision of real-time reporting capabilities that allow for timely adjustments to media strategies based on up-to-date performance data. The modular configuration of the system further allows for scalability and adaptability to accommodate additional media sources, web tracking sources, or reporting requirements as needed.

# Method and System for Attributing Web-Based Orders to Media Advertisements

## Background of the Invention

Advertisers who deploy media advertisements—such as television commercials, radio spots, or streaming audio/video advertisements—face a persistent and growing challenge in accurately attributing consumer responses to specific advertisement airings. While traditional direct-response advertising relied on unique phone numbers or promotional codes to track conversions, the modern consumer journey frequently involves a viewer seeing a media advertisement and subsequently navigating to a website via a search engine, direct navigation, or a mobile device, rather than calling a designated phone number.

This shift in consumer behavior has created a significant attribution gap. Advertisers invest substantial budgets in media campaigns across numerous networks, stations, and dayparts, yet lack the technical means to determine which specific airing—defined by its particular date, time, network, and creative version—resulted in a specific web-based order or conversion event. Existing analytics solutions typically rely on manual correlation, broad time-window heuristics, or self-reported attribution surveys, all of which are imprecise, labor-intensive, and unable to scale across high-volume, multi-network media campaigns.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention overcomes these limitations by providing a specifically programmed server system configured to automatically and periodically retrieve two distinct categories of data from multiple disparate sources over a computer network: (1) media airing data, which includes detailed records of when and where specific advertisements were broadcast or streamed, including network identifiers, air dates, air times, creative/spot identifiers, and market or station information; and (2) web tracking transaction data, which comprises records of web-based orders, including timestamps, session identifiers, referral sources, geographic data, and transaction details captured by website tracking pixels, tags, or server-side logging mechanisms.

The server is programmed with matching logic and algorithms that process these two data streams in order to computationally determine, for each individual web order, the specific media airing most likely responsible for generating that order. This matching process may account for temporal proximity between an airing and a subsequent order, geographic correlation between the market in which an advertisement aired and the location associated with the web order, statistical baseline modeling to distinguish incremental lift from ordinary web traffic, and other configurable attribution rules or weighting factors.

Because the server is programmed to periodically poll and ingest new airing data and new transaction data as they become available—rather than requiring a static, one-time batch upload—the system is capable of continuously updating its attribution determinations. As new web orders are received, they are automatically matched against the most recent media airing data. As new airing data becomes available, previously unmatched or provisionally matched orders may be re-evaluated and reattributed accordingly.

The output of this automated matching process is compiled into an attribution report that is dynamically and automatically updatable in substantially real time. This report presents advertisers with a data-driven view of cross-channel campaign performance, enabling them to observe which specific media placements are driving measurable web-based conversions. Unlike static, manually generated reports, the attribution report of the present invention reflects the most current available data at any given time, allowing advertisers to make timely, informed decisions regarding media buying, creative optimization, and budget allocation.

## Detailed Description of Exemplary Embodiments

### System Architecture

In an exemplary embodiment, the invention is implemented as a networked computing system comprising one or more specifically programmed servers, one or more databases for storing airing data and transaction data, and a plurality of network interfaces configured to communicate with external data sources over the internet or other computer networks.

The server may be configured to establish periodic connections—via scheduled polling, application programming interface (API) calls, file transfer protocols, or webhook-based push notifications—with:

- **Media monitoring services** that track and log advertisement airings across television, radio, and streaming platforms, providing granular data such as network, station, market, air date, air time, and unique spot or creative identifiers;
- **Website tracking systems**, including tracking pixels embedded in advertiser websites, tag management systems, e-commerce platforms, and web analytics servers, which record web-based orders along with associated metadata such as timestamp, session duration, referral information, IP-derived geographic data, and order value.

### Data Collection and Normalization

Upon retrieval, the server is programmed to normalize the disparate data formats received from multiple third-party sources into a standardized internal data structure. This normalization step accounts for variations in time zone reporting, data granularity, and identifier schemes used by different media monitoring services and web tracking platforms, ensuring that airing data and transaction data can be accurately compared and correlated regardless of their original source format.

### Matching and Attribution Engine

The core matching engine of the server applies one or more attribution algorithms to associate individual web orders with specific media airings. In one embodiment, the matching engine evaluates the time elapsed between an airing and a subsequent web order within a defined attribution window, giving greater weight to orders occurring shortly after an airing. In another embodiment, the matching engine incorporates geographic correlation, cross-referencing the designated market area (DMA) or broadcast region of an airing with the geographic origin of the web order.

The matching engine may further employ statistical modeling techniques, such as baseline traffic estimation, to distinguish web orders that represent incremental conversions attributable to a specific airing from orders that would have occurred regardless of the advertisement. Machine learning models may optionally be trained on historical matched data to improve the accuracy of future attribution determinations, adjusting weighting factors based on observed patterns in consumer response times, order values, and channel-specific behavior.

### Real-Time Report Generation

Once individual web orders have been matched to their corresponding media airings, the server generates an attribution report accessible to advertisers via a web-based dashboard, downloadable file, or API endpoint. This report may present data at varying levels of granularity, including:

- Aggregate performance metrics by network, station, daypart, or creative version;
- Individual matched order details, including the specific airing responsible for each conversion;
- Return-on-investment calculations correlating media spend with attributed web-based revenue;
- Trend analysis illustrating attribution performance over time.

Because the underlying server continuously ingests new airing and transaction data, the attribution report is not a static snapshot but rather a continuously refreshed representation of campaign performance. As additional data becomes available, the server automatically recalculates and updates the report, ensuring that advertisers always have access to the most current and accurate attribution insights available.

### Advantages of the Invention

The system described herein provides numerous advantages over conventional attribution methods. By automating the collection, normalization, and matching of media airing and web transaction data, the invention eliminates the need for labor-intensive manual correlation processes. The real-time updatable nature of the attribution report allows advertisers to make prompt, data-driven adjustments to their media strategies, rather than relying on delayed or outdated performance summaries. Furthermore, the system's ability to draw from multiple, disparate third-party data sources ensures broad applicability across diverse advertising ecosystems, including television, radio, and streaming media, thereby providing a comprehensive, cross-channel view of advertising effectiveness that has not been achievable through prior art solutions.

# PATENT APPLICATION CLAIMS

## SYSTEM CLAIMS

**Claim 1.** A system for real-time attribution of web-based conversion events to media advertisement airings, the system comprising:

a media monitoring module configured to receive broadcast schedule data and detect airing events, each airing event comprising a media asset identifier, a broadcast channel identifier, and an airing timestamp;

a data ingestion module configured to receive, in real time, a plurality of web conversion events from one or more web servers, each web conversion event comprising a timestamp, a source identifier, and conversion metadata;

a temporal correlation engine configured to:
   (a) define a plurality of attribution windows, each attribution window associated with a respective airing event and having a start time based on the airing timestamp and a duration determined based on at least one of: historical response-time data, media asset duration, or channel-specific response profiles;
   (b) identify, for each web conversion event, one or more candidate airing events having an attribution window encompassing the timestamp of the web conversion event; and
   (c) calculate an attribution score for each candidate airing event based on a temporal proximity between the web conversion event timestamp and the airing timestamp;

a statistical baseline module configured to compute an expected baseline conversion rate for a time period independent of airing events, based on historical conversion data;

an incrementality determination module configured to calculate an incremental lift value by comparing an observed conversion rate during an attribution window to the expected baseline conversion rate; and

an output module configured to generate, in real time, an attribution record associating the web conversion event with a specific airing event, the attribution record comprising the attribution score and the incremental lift value.

---

**Claim 2.** The system of claim 1, wherein the temporal correlation engine is further configured to adjust the duration of an attribution window dynamically based on a detected surge in web conversion events following the airing timestamp.

**Claim 3.** The system of claim 1, wherein the attribution score is calculated using a decay function that reduces the attribution score as the temporal proximity between the web conversion event and the airing timestamp increases.

**Claim 4.** The system of claim 1, wherein the source identifier comprises at least one of: a vanity URL, a promotional code, a UTM parameter, a device identifier, or an IP-address-derived geographic region.

**Claim 5.** The system of claim 1, wherein the media monitoring module is configured to detect the airing event using automatic content recognition (ACR) applied to a broadcast audio or video signal.

**Claim 6.** The system of claim 1, further comprising a multi-touch resolution module configured to, upon identifying a plurality of candidate airing events for a single web conversion event, allocate fractional attribution credit among the plurality of candidate airing events based on a weighting algorithm.

**Claim 7.** The system of claim 6, wherein the weighting algorithm allocates attribution credit based on at least one of: recency of each candidate airing event, media channel priority, or historical channel-specific conversion probability.

**Claim 8.** The system of claim 1, wherein the incrementality determination module is further configured to compare the observed conversion rate against a plurality of geographically segmented control regions in which the airing event was not broadcast.

**Claim 9.** The system of claim 1, further comprising a real-time feedback module configured to transmit the attribution record to a media buying platform to adjust future media placement in less than a threshold time period from the airing event.

**Claim 10.** The system of claim 1, wherein the data ingestion module is configured to receive the web conversion events via a streaming data pipeline having an end-to-end latency of less than a specified threshold from event occurrence to attribution record generation.

---

## METHOD CLAIMS

**Claim 11.** A computer-implemented method for real-time attribution of web conversion events to media advertisement airings, the method comprising:

receiving, by one or more processors, data indicating an airing event of a media advertisement, the data comprising an airing timestamp and a media identifier;

establishing, by the one or more processors, an attribution window associated with the airing event, the attribution window defining a time interval following the airing timestamp;

receiving, in real time, a stream of web conversion events, each web conversion event comprising an event timestamp;

determining, for each web conversion event, whether the event timestamp falls within the attribution window;

responsive to determining that the event timestamp falls within the attribution window, calculating an attribution score representing a likelihood that the web conversion event resulted from the airing event, wherein the attribution score is calculated based at least in part on a temporal distance between the event timestamp and the airing timestamp;

computing an incremental lift metric by comparing a conversion rate observed within the attribution window to a baseline conversion rate computed from a period absent the airing event; and

generating and transmitting, within a predetermined latency threshold from the web conversion event, an attribution record linking the web conversion event to the airing event.

**Claim 12.** The method of claim 11, further comprising:

detecting a plurality of airing events occurring within overlapping or sequential time periods; and

apportioning attribution credit for a given web conversion event across the plurality of airing events according to a multi-touch attribution model.

**Claim 13.** The method of claim 11, further comprising dynamically adjusting the attribution window based on real-time observation of a conversion event volume exceeding a threshold rate following the airing timestamp.

**Claim 14.** The method of claim 11, wherein establishing the attribution window comprises retrieving a historical response curve associated with the media identifier and setting the time interval based on a percentile of the historical response curve.

**Claim 15.** The method of claim 11, further comprising suppressing generation of the attribution record when the incremental lift metric falls below a predetermined significance threshold.

**Claim 16.** The method of claim 11, further comprising normalizing the baseline conversion rate based on at least one of: day-of-week seasonality, time-of-day seasonality, or concurrent marketing activity across other channels.

**Claim 17.** The method of claim 11, wherein generating the attribution record further comprises calculating a media spend efficiency metric based on the attribution score and a cost associated with the airing event.

---

## COMPUTER-READABLE MEDIUM CLAIM

**Claim 18.** A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations comprising:

receiving airing event data comprising an airing timestamp and a media asset identifier;

ingesting a real-time stream of web conversion events;

correlating each web conversion event with one or more candidate airing events based on a time-windowed comparison between the web conversion event timestamp and the airing timestamp;

computing an attribution score for each correlation based on temporal proximity;

determining an incremental conversion lift by statistically comparing observed conversion volume to a modeled baseline; and

outputting an attribution record within a real-time latency constraint, the attribution record usable to adjust ongoing media buying decisions.

**Claim 19.** The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 18, wherein the operations further comprise validating the attribution score using an A/B test in which the media advertisement is withheld from a control audience segment.

**Claim 20.** The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 18, wherein the operations further comprise detecting anomalous conversion patterns indicative of fraudulent conversion events and excluding such events from the incremental conversion lift computation.

---

Additional independent claims directed to specific novel algorithmic components (e.g., the decay-function attribution scoring or the dynamic window adjustment) may be warranted depending on prior art search results. Consider adding claims directed to a graphical user interface displaying real-time attribution dashboards if disclosed in the specification.]*

# Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a server-based system and method for attributing orders and conversions to specific advertisements by ingesting, correlating, and analyzing media airing data and web tracking data. In accordance with one aspect of the invention, a computer system comprising one or more processors and associated memory is configured to receive, over one or more networks, media airing data from one or more media monitoring sources, wherein the media airing data comprises information identifying a plurality of advertisements broadcast, streamed, or otherwise distributed across one or more media channels, together with associated metadata including, without limitation, an identifier of the advertisement, an identifier of the media channel or station, a broadcast date and time, a duration, and a market or geographic designation.

The system is further configured to receive, over the one or more networks, web tracking data generated by one or more client devices interacting with a website, mobile application, or other online property associated with an advertiser. The web tracking data comprises a plurality of events, including without limitation page views, session initiations, and completed orders, each of which is associated with a timestamp, a session identifier, and, where available, one or more attribution parameters such as a referring source, a promotional code, or a geographic indicator derived from an internet protocol address or other location-determining mechanism.

According to a further aspect of the invention, the system comprises an attribution engine configured to correlate the media airing data with the web tracking data based upon one or more temporal, geographic, and/or behavioral criteria in order to attribute a given order or conversion event to a specific advertisement airing. In one embodiment, the attribution engine identifies a time window following the airing of an advertisement in a given market and determines whether one or more orders originating from that market fall within the time window, thereby establishing a candidate association between the advertisement and the order. In another embodiment, the attribution engine applies a statistical or probabilistic model, such as a baseline-and-lift model, to distinguish order activity attributable to the airing of the advertisement from order activity attributable to organic or background demand, by comparing observed order volumes during and following the airing to a baseline order volume established during periods absent the airing.

In accordance with a further aspect of the invention, the system may incorporate weighting or scoring logic that accounts for one or more factors influencing the likelihood of a causal relationship between an advertisement airing and an order, including without limitation the elapsed time between the airing and the order, the media channel and program context, the advertisement's historical performance, the presence of matching promotional identifiers, and the geographic proximity between the airing market and the location associated with the order. The attribution engine may aggregate a plurality of candidate associations and apply a fractional or weighted attribution methodology such that a single order may be attributed, in whole or in part, to more than one advertisement airing.

The system further comprises a reporting module configured to generate one or more performance metrics for a given advertisement, media channel, program, or campaign based upon the attributed orders, including without limitation a response rate, a cost per order, a return on advertising spend, and a lift metric reflecting the incremental order volume attributable to the advertisement airing relative to the established baseline. The reporting module may present such metrics via a graphical user interface, an application programming interface, or an automatically generated report, and may further provide the metrics substantially in real time or on a periodic or on-demand basis.

In certain embodiments, the system is configured to receive media airing data and web tracking data from a plurality of disparate and heterogeneous sources, to normalize such data into a common data structure or schema, and to store the normalized data in one or more databases for subsequent retrieval and analysis by the attribution engine. The system may further comprise one or more machine learning models trained upon historical airing data, web tracking data, and known or previously attributed orders, such that the attribution engine improves in accuracy over time as additional data is ingested.

It is to be understood that the foregoing summary describes certain illustrative embodiments and aspects of the invention and is not intended to limit the scope of the invention, which is defined by the claims appended hereto. Additional features, advantages, and embodiments of the invention are set forth in, or will be apparent from, the detailed description, drawings, and claims that follow.

# Patent-Style Boilerplate: Media Attribution Platform

**SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR CORRELATING MEDIA CREATIVE AIRINGS WITH RESULTING WEB-BASED TRANSACTIONS**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to media measurement and attribution systems, and more particularly to systems and methods for correlating the airing of creative content (e.g., television, streaming, radio, or digital advertisements) with subsequent user-initiated web transactions, thereby enabling attribution of downstream conversion events to specific media exposures.

---

## BACKGROUND

Advertisers and media buyers routinely deploy creative assets across multiple channels and platforms with the goal of driving measurable consumer action, such as website visits, purchases, sign-ups, or other conversion events. Conventional attribution methods often rely on last-click models, cookie-based tracking, or self-reported survey data, each of which suffers from limitations including latency, incomplete cross-channel visibility, privacy-driven signal loss, and an inability to isolate the causal impact of a specific airing event.

There exists a need for systems capable of ingesting granular airing data (including timestamp, channel, network, creative identifier, and geographic distribution) and correlating that data, in near-real-time or retrospectively, with web transaction logs to produce statistically robust attribution signals.

---

## SUMMARY

In one embodiment, a system is provided comprising:

(a) an **airing ingestion module** configured to receive metadata associated with the broadcast or transmission of a creative asset, including but not limited to airing timestamp, duration, network/channel identifier, geographic market, and creative/asset identifier;

(b) a **transaction ingestion module** configured to receive event data associated with web-based user transactions, including but not limited to session timestamp, referring domain, conversion type, transaction value, and anonymized or pseudonymized user/session identifiers;

(c) a **correlation engine** configured to apply one or more temporal, geographic, and/or statistical models to associate a given airing event with a resulting lift or change in transaction volume within a defined attribution window;

(d) a **normalization module** configured to account for baseline transaction activity absent media exposure, seasonality, and confounding concurrent campaigns; and

(e) a **reporting interface** configured to output attribution scores, incremental lift metrics, and/or return-on-investment calculations attributable to individual airings or aggregated campaigns.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION (Illustrative)

### 1. System Architecture

Referring to FIG. 1, the media attribution platform (100) comprises an airing data source (110), a transaction data source (120), a correlation engine (130), a data store (140), and a user-facing reporting dashboard (150).

The airing data source (110) may include feeds from television monitoring services, ad-serving platforms, streaming platform APIs, or radio monitoring services, each providing structured or semi-structured metadata regarding the time, place, and content of a given creative airing.

The transaction data source (120) may include web server logs, e-commerce platform APIs, CRM export data, or tag-based pixel events reflecting user actions taken on a target website or application.

### 2. Correlation Methodology

In one embodiment, the correlation engine (130) implements a time-windowed lift analysis, wherein transaction volume in a defined post-airing window (e.g., 0–30 minutes, 0–24 hours) is compared against a statistically modeled baseline derived from historical transaction patterns absent the airing event. Divergence from baseline within the window is attributed, in whole or in part, to the airing event, subject to confidence thresholds.

In another embodiment, geographic matching is employed, wherein airing distribution footprints (e.g., designated market areas, zip codes) are cross-referenced against the geographic origin of transaction events (e.g., IP-derived or device-reported location) to isolate correlated activity within the exposed population relative to a non-exposed control population.

In yet another embodiment, a machine learning model is trained on historical pairs of (airing features, transaction outcomes) to predict expected incremental transaction lift as a function of creative attributes, air time, network, and market, with model output continuously refined via feedback from observed outcomes.

### 3. Attribution Scoring

The normalization module (135) may apply adjustments for:
- Known concurrent media activity across other channels;
- Seasonal or day-of-week transaction baselines;
- Statistical noise thresholds below which lift is not attributed;
- Multi-touch weighting where multiple airings precede a single transaction.

Output of the correlation engine may include an attribution score, a confidence interval, and/or a computed marginal return on ad spend (ROAS) for the associated creative or campaign.

### 4. Optional Features

- Real-time or near-real-time processing pipeline (e.g., streaming ingestion via message queue architecture) to support rapid iterative campaign optimization.
- Privacy-preserving aggregation techniques (e.g., differential privacy, k-anonymity thresholds) applied prior to output where user-level data is involved.
- API layer enabling third-party demand-side platforms (DSPs) or media buying systems to ingest attribution scores for automated bid or spend adjustment.

---

## EXAMPLE CLAIMS (Illustrative Only)

**Claim 1.** A computer-implemented method for correlating media creative airings with web-based transactions, comprising:

receiving, by one or more processors, airing data associated with a transmission of a creative asset, the airing data comprising at least a timestamp and a geographic distribution indicator;

receiving, by the one or more processors, transaction data associated with one or more web-based transactions, the transaction data comprising at least a transaction timestamp and a geographic origin indicator;

determining, by the one or more processors, a temporal window following the airing data timestamp;

identifying, within the temporal window, a subset of the transaction data exhibiting statistically significant deviation from a baseline transaction volume; and

generating an attribution score associating the subset of transaction data with the creative asset.

**Claim 2.** The method of claim 1, further comprising normalizing the attribution score based on concurrent media activity occurring within the temporal window.

# SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR REAL-TIME MULTI-CHANNEL MEDIA ATTRIBUTION

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present disclosure relates generally to computer-implemented systems for marketing analytics, and more particularly to systems and methods for collecting, synchronizing, and correlating media airing data with web tracking data to generate real-time attribution reports quantifying the impact of media broadcasts on digital consumer behavior.

## BACKGROUND

[0002] Advertisers expend substantial resources broadcasting media content across television, radio, streaming, and other linear and digital channels. A persistent challenge in the industry is measuring the causal or correlative impact of such media airings on subsequent consumer actions, such as website visits, search queries, or conversion events. Conventional analytics platforms typically operate in isolated data silos: broadcast monitoring services track when and where advertisements air, while web analytics platforms independently track visitor behavior on a given domain. These systems generally lack the capability to synchronize disparate data streams in real time, normalize timestamps across heterogeneous sources, and computationally attribute observed web traffic surges to specific media airing events with sufficient granularity and speed to enable actionable decision-making.

[0003] Existing attribution approaches often rely on batch processing performed hours or days after an airing event, rendering the resulting insights unsuitable for time-sensitive applications such as dynamic ad buying, real-time campaign adjustment, or immediate performance validation. Furthermore, prior systems frequently require manual correlation of airing logs against web analytics exports, introducing latency, human error, and an inability to scale across large numbers of concurrent media placements.

[0004] There exists a need for an automated, computer-implemented system capable of ingesting media airing data and web tracking data from multiple heterogeneous sources, normalizing and time-aligning such data, and generating attribution reports in real time or near-real time, thereby enabling advertisers to assess and act upon the performance of media investments with minimal latency.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] The present disclosure describes a computer-implemented system and associated methods for real-time media attribution, comprising, in various embodiments, a media airing data collection module, a web tracking data collection module, a data synchronization and normalization engine, an attribution processing engine, and a reporting and visualization module. The system is configured to ingest media airing events from one or more broadcast monitoring sources, ingest web traffic and engagement events from one or more tracked digital properties, align these data streams temporally and contextually, compute statistically significant attribution metrics correlating media airings to observed changes in web activity, and present the resulting attribution data through a real-time reporting interface.

[0006] In one embodiment, the system comprises one or more processors, network interfaces, and non-transitory computer-readable storage media storing instructions that, when executed, cause the system to perform the operations described herein. The modular architecture disclosed permits scalability across large numbers of concurrent media campaigns and tracked web properties, and supports configurable attribution windows, baseline modeling techniques, and confidence-scoring mechanisms.

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0007] FIG. 1 illustrates a block diagram of the overall system architecture, including the media airing data collection module, web tracking data collection module, synchronization engine, attribution engine, and reporting module, according to an embodiment.

[0008] FIG. 2 illustrates a data flow diagram depicting the ingestion, normalization, and correlation of media airing events and web tracking events, according to an embodiment.

[0009] FIG. 3 illustrates a flowchart of the attribution scoring process, including baseline traffic modeling and lift calculation, according to an embodiment.

[0010] FIG. 4 illustrates an exemplary real-time attribution dashboard generated by the reporting and visualization module, according to an embodiment.

[0011] FIG. 5 illustrates a sequence diagram showing the timing relationship between an airing event, data collection latency, and attribution report generation, according to an embodiment.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### I. System Overview

[0012] Referring to FIG. 1, the system 100 comprises a plurality of interconnected functional modules operating on one or more computing devices, which may include physical servers, virtualized cloud computing instances, or a distributed computing cluster. The system 100 includes a media airing data collection module 110, a web tracking data collection module 120, a data synchronization and normalization engine 130, an attribution processing engine 140, a reporting and visualization module 150, and a data storage layer 160 comprising one or more databases or data warehouses.

[0013] The modules communicate via one or more internal message buses, application programming interfaces (APIs), or network protocols, and may be deployed across a distributed architecture to support horizontal scaling and fault tolerance. Each module is described in detail below.

### II. Media Airing Data Collection Module

[0014] The media airing data collection module 110 is configured to receive, retrieve, or otherwise obtain data records corresponding to instances of media content broadcast across one or more channels, including but not limited to television broadcast, radio broadcast, over-the-top (OTT) streaming platforms, satellite media, podcast platforms, and digital audio/video advertising networks.

[0015] In one embodiment, the module 110 comprises:

(a) one or more **ingestion connectors** 111 configured to interface with third-party broadcast monitoring services, automatic content recognition (ACR) systems, set-top box data providers, or direct feeds from media traffic and billing systems, each such connector configured to receive airing event data comprising at minimum a station or channel identifier, a timestamp indicating the airing start time, an airing duration, a creative or advertisement identifier, and a geographic market designation;

(b) a **normalization sub-module** 112 configured to convert incoming airing records from heterogeneous source-specific formats into a canonical internal data schema, including conversion of timestamps to a common time reference (e.g., Coordinated Universal Time) and mapping of source-specific market or station codes to a standardized taxonomy;

(c) a **deduplication sub-module** 113 configured to identify and merge duplicate airing records received from multiple overlapping monitoring sources, using matching criteria comprising creative identifier, timestamp proximity within a configurable tolerance window, and channel identifier; and

(d) an **event queue** 114 configured to buffer normalized airing events for consumption by the data synchronization and normalization engine 130, wherein the event queue 114 supports publish-subscribe semantics to enable low-latency delivery of airing events as they are received.

[0016] In an embodiment, the ingestion connectors 111 poll external data sources at a configurable interval (e.g., every 1 to 60 seconds), or alternatively subscribe to webhook-based push notifications provided by third-party monitoring services, such that airing events are made available to downstream modules within a latency target of less than a specified number of seconds from actual broadcast time.

### III. Web Tracking Data Collection Module

[0017] The web tracking data collection module 120 is configured to collect data indicative of visitor interactions with one or more tracked digital properties, such as websites, mobile applications, or landing pages associated with an advertiser's media campaigns.

[0018] In one embodiment, the module 120 comprises:

(a) a **client-side tracking script or software development kit (SDK)** 121 deployed on the tracked digital property, configured to capture events including, without limitation, page views, session initiations, referral source, geographic location derived from IP address or device data, search queries, form submissions, and conversion events, and to transmit such events to the system 100 via HTTPS or other secure transport protocol;

(b) a **server-side event receiver** 122 configured to receive the transmitted event data, validate the data against an expected schema, and enrich the data with metadata including a normalized timestamp, an assigned session identifier, and a geographic market designation derived from the visitor's IP address or other location signal;

(c) a **traffic aggregation sub-module** 123 configured to compute rolling aggregate metrics, including but not limited to visits per unit time, unique visitors per unit time, and conversion events per unit time, segmented by geographic market and by referral channel; and

(d) an **event queue** 124, structurally and functionally analogous to event queue 114, configured to buffer normalized web tracking events and aggregate metrics for consumption by the data synchronization and normalization engine 130.

[0019] In an embodiment, the geographic market designation computed in sub-module 122 is derived using an IP-to-market mapping database configured to associate visitor IP addresses with designated market areas (DMAs) or other broadcast market taxonomies, thereby enabling correlation between web traffic originating in a given market and media airings broadcast within that same market.

### IV. Data Synchronization and Normalization Engine

[0020] Referring to FIG. 2, the data synchronization and normalization engine 130 is configured to consume normalized event streams from the event queues 114 and 124, and to align such streams along a common temporal and geographic reference frame.

[0021] In one embodiment, the engine 130 comprises:

(a) a **time alignment sub-module** 131 configured to bucket both airing events and web tracking events into discrete time intervals (e.g., one-minute or five-minute windows) according to a shared clock reference;

(b) a **market alignment sub-module** 132 configured to associate each airing event with the one or more designated market areas in which the airing occurred, and to associate each web traffic aggregate with the designated market area from which the traffic originated, thereby enabling market-level correlation;

(c) a **unified event store** 133, implemented within the data storage layer 160, configured to persist time-aligned and market-aligned airing events and web traffic aggregates in a schema optimized for time-series querying; and

(d) a **stream processing controller** 134 configured to orchestrate the continuous, low-latency flow of data from the event queues 114, 124 into the unified event store 133, utilizing a distributed stream processing framework configured for at-least-once or exactly-once delivery semantics.

### V. Attribution Processing Engine

[0022] Referring to FIG. 3, the attribution processing engine 140 is configured to computationally determine the degree to which observed web traffic in a given time interval and market is attributable to one or more media airing events.

[0023] In one embodiment, the engine 140 comprises:

(a) a **baseline modeling sub-module** 141 configured to compute an expected or predicted level of web traffic for a given market and time interval in the absence of a media airing event, using one or more of: historical traffic averages for corresponding time-of-day and day-of-week periods, exponential smoothing models, autoregressive statistical models, or machine-learned regression models trained on historical traffic patterns;

(b) a **lift calculation sub-module** 142 configured to compute an observed lift value representing the difference, or normalized difference, between actual observed web traffic and the baseline traffic predicted by sub-module 141, for a time window beginning at or after a given airing event and extending for a configurable attribution window duration (e.g., 1 to 30 minutes post-airing);

(c) a **attribution confidence scoring sub-module** 143 configured to compute a statistical confidence score or significance measure associated with the computed lift value, accounting for factors including but not limited to baseline variance, the presence of temporally overlapping airing events from the same or competing advertisers, and historical correlation strength for the given creative, channel, and market combination;

(d) a **multi-touch allocation sub-module** 144, configured, in embodiments involving multiple temporally proximate airing events, to allocate a fractional attribution credit to each of a plurality of candidate airing events using a weighting methodology comprising one or more of: time-decay weighting, position-based weighting, or a data-driven weighting model trained on historical attribution outcomes; and

(e) an **attribution record generator** 145 configured to produce a structured attribution record for each processed airing event, the record comprising the airing event identifier, the computed lift value, the associated confidence score, the attributed market, and the attribution window utilized.

# Summary of the Invention

In some embodiments, the present invention is directed to a system and method for advertising attribution analytics that captures, processes, and analyzes user interaction data across multiple digital touchpoints to determine the relative contribution of each marketing channel, campaign, or advertisement to a resulting conversion event. In some embodiments, the system comprises one or more processors configured to receive event data from a plurality of disparate data sources, including but not limited to web analytics platforms, mobile application software development kits (SDKs), customer relationship management (CRM) systems, and third-party advertising networks. In some embodiments, the system generates a unified user identifier configured to probabilistically or deterministically link interactions occurring across multiple devices and sessions to a single user journey. In some embodiments, the system applies one or more attribution models, selected from a group comprising first-touch attribution, last-touch attribution, linear attribution, time-decay attribution, position-based attribution, and a data-driven attribution model generated using a machine learning algorithm trained on historical conversion data, to assign a weighted attribution value to each touchpoint within the user journey. In some embodiments, the machine learning algorithm is configured to dynamically adjust attribution weights based on detected patterns in conversion likelihood associated with specific touchpoint sequences, channel combinations, and temporal spacing between interactions. In some embodiments, the system further comprises a reporting module configured to generate a graphical user interface displaying attribution results, return on advertising spend (ROAS) metrics, and comparative channel performance data in real time or near-real time. In some embodiments, the system is configured to detect and filter fraudulent or non-human interaction data prior to attribution calculation using one or more anomaly detection techniques. In some embodiments, the attribution data generated by the system is used to automatically adjust bidding parameters, budget allocation, or campaign targeting parameters across one or more connected advertising platforms via an application programming interface (API) integration, thereby improving the efficiency and accuracy of digital advertising spend allocation.
